children: London cocoa turned lower on Tuesday, after climbing to a one-year peak earlier, with the main crop season due to start in top grower Ivory Coast, while robusta coffee set a 2-1/2 month low.
fell 0.5% to £4,833 a metric ton by 1112 GMT after setting a one-year high of £4,988 earlier in the session.

* Dealers noted a strengthening El Nino weather event could contribute to a fall in production in Ivory Coast although there may still be a global surplus in 2026/27 albeit a much smaller one than in the previous season.

* Rains were below average last week in most of Ivory Coast's cocoa-growing regions, farmers said on Monday, warning that persistent dry weather could damage and shorten the September-to-February main crop.
lost 2.8% to $3,431 a ton after setting a 2-1/2 month low of $3,428 earlier in the session.
* Dealers said the robusta market currently had ample supplies with exports from top producer Vietnam running ahead of last year's pace.

* The outlook for global coffee supply looks comfortable, but harvest delays in Brazil and earthquake-linked problems in Colombia have slowed down the flow of beans from producing to consuming countries, Dutch bank Rabobank said on Monday.
* However, dealers said tight supplies and strong domestic prices in top consumer India was helping underpin prices.
* India reduced sugar stock holding limits for dealers to 2,000 quintals, from 4,000 quintals earlier, effective from September 15 until November 30, the government said in a statement on Tuesday.
